title: Classiq Updates Qmod Compiler to Synthesize 2048-Bit Shor’s Algorithm in Under 10 Seconds - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Classiq has introduced architectural upgrades to its Qmod quantum programming language and synthesis compiler that enable the period-finding subroutine of Shor’s algorithm for a 2048-bit RSA-scale integer to compile in under ten seconds. Detailed in a technical post by Classiq’s Matan Vax, the release addresses a long-standing bottleneck in fault-tolerant quantum software tooling, where flat circuit representations unroll classical loops and duplicate subroutines, causing synthesis runtimes and program sizes to blow up as qubit counts grow.

Rather than flattening circuits, the updated Qmod compiler preserves classical control structures—including repeat, foreach, and conditional blocks—throughout synthesis and permits classical iteration variables to symbolically index quantum qubit arrays. This symbolic indexing allows built-in arithmetic modules, Quantum Fourier Transforms, and Quantum Phase Estimation routines to synthesize in nearly constant time with respect to operand width, while keeping the coprime base a as a runtime execution parameter so a single compiled program can be reused across multiple Shor iterations.
